final_response:
The SNR (power ratio) is $400$, and $\mathrm{SNR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 26.0\ \mathrm{dB}$.

\boxed{400,\ 26.0\ \mathrm{dB}}

**Derivation:**

Since power is proportional to voltage squared ($P = V^2/R$) across the same impedance, the signal-to-noise power ratio is the square of the voltage ratio:

$$\mathrm{SNR} = \frac{P_s}{P_n} = \left(\frac{V_s}{V_n}\right)^2 = 20^2 = 400$$

Converting to decibels:

$$\mathrm{SNR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 10\log_{10}(400) = 20\log_{10}(20) \approx 20 \times 1.30103 = 26.0206\ \mathrm{dB}$$

Rounded to 3 significant figures: $26.0\ \mathrm{dB}$.
